name: The Bible Never Says Jesus Was Born on 25 December

beats.say: The Bible never says Jesus was born on December 25th. So who picked the date?
Matthew and Luke, the two books that tell His birth, give no date. Not even a month.
The first record of a December 25th Christmas comes from Rome, for the year 336. Three centuries later.
Why that day? Historians still argue. Some point to a Roman sun festival. Others to early Christian date math.
The date was never the point. The birth was. Luke 2, verse 11:
"For there is born to you this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord."

post.yt_title: Was Jesus Born on 25 December? The Bible Never Says 🎄 #shorts
post.yt_desc:
The Bible never says Jesus was born on December 25th. Matthew and Luke, the two Gospels that tell His birth, give no date, not even a month. The first record of Christians marking 25 December comes from Rome, in a list for the year 336, about three centuries later. Why that day? Historians still debate it: some point to a Roman sun festival, others to early Christian date calculations.

But the date was never the point. The birth was: "For there is born to you this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord" (Luke 2:11 NKJV). "But when the fullness of the time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman" (Galatians 4:4 NKJV).

📖 Read it yourself: Matthew 1:18–2:12 · Luke 2:1–20 · Galatians 4:4–5 (NKJV)

post.notes:
- No date or month for Jesus' birth in Matthew 1-2 or Luke 1-2 (the only two birth narratives).
- Earliest record: the Chronograph (Calendar) of 354, compiled in Rome, whose Depositio Martyrum list (reflecting the year 336) begins with 'VIII kal. Ian. natus Christus in Betleem Iudeae' (25 December). Commonly summarized as the first record of a 25 December Nativity feast, for AD 336.
- Origin debated: the 'History of Religions' theory (linked to the Roman sun festival, Sol Invictus / 25 Dec as winter solstice in the Julian calendar) vs the 'Calculation' theory (25 March conception + 9 months). Both stated as theories only.
- Luke 2:11 NKJV (bible.com v114): "For there is born to you this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord." Full verse. Spoken by an angel to shepherds near Bethlehem (Luke 2:8-10); 'city of David' = Bethlehem (Luke 2:4).
- Galatians 4:4 NKJV: "But when the fullness of the time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the law," Quoted from "when" to "woman"; … at both ends.
- 'Enjoy the 25th' is not a doctrinal claim; respectful of all Christmas traditions.
